feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital communications and credible progression at NACo. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly dense, somewhat repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by adding more outcomes and trimming overlap.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear professional brand: the headline, summary, and experience consistently position you as a digital strategy/communications leader with technical depth.  
- Credible career progression: multiple promotions within one organization strengthen trust and show increasing scope, leadership, and responsibility.  
- Good use of scale indicators: metrics like 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million page views, and 50+ publishers add weight and specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and make the CV feel tighter.  
- Add stronger outcome language: several bullets describe responsibilities more than results. Where possible, quantify improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, revenue, or campaign performance.  
- Minor writing/style fixes: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; make comma usage consistent in lists (“workflows and systems” vs. “workflows, systems”); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns with the CV’s direction, but it reads a bit generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with sharper positioning tied to recent leadership in digital transformation, governance, and public-sector/advocacy communications.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations leadership.
- Add public-sector/association context to reflect the strongest recent experience and improve relevance.
- Tighten broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” into a more executive summary.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and membership organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, Drupal and CMS modernization, editorial workflows, and digital governance. Strong background in advocacy and public-sector communications, stakeholder coordination, and translating complex policy or technical topics into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies/Soft Skills.
- Avoid overloading the intro with tools or channel lists already detailed elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value, senior-level capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, leadership-level language: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “Web platform modernization,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Reduce overlap and improve parallel structure; suggested version: Digital transformation strategy • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics & performance reporting • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Advocacy & policy communications • Stakeholder coordination • Multimedia & live event production
- Standardize style: use “communications” instead of “communication” for consistency with the rest of the CV.
- Consider ordering by relevance/seniority: strategy, platforms, governance/workflows, analytics, communications, production.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates the header and Soft Skills section.
- Several items substantially repeat Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, analytics, multimedia, and workflow/governance themes.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership language: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate bullets by theme: 1) enterprise web/content operations, 2) Drupal campaign/microsite delivery, 3) cross-channel governance/usability, 4) AI search initiative.
- Add measurable detail where possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital systems, workflows and analytics” and “governance/usability best practices” repeat NACo and the summary; keep only if tied to new outcomes.
- AI-enabled search and microsite work already appears in Recent Projects, so this entry should emphasize leadership, scope, and business impact rather than project detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more specific or results-based: add email list size, engagement growth, campaign performance, production volume, or cost/time savings from the studio and analytics stack.
- Tighten softer bullets: replace “strengthened”/“improving” with concrete outcomes such as faster publishing, better reporting cadence, clearer ownership, reduced bottlenecks, or increased in-house production capacity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version at a more strategic/enterprise level.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries; emphasize building the studio and scaling organizational capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you owned at this level: executional leadership, recurring products, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video bullet: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one outcome-oriented line: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” is already stated in the Director role; keep this version focused on day-to-day operations rather than team-wide leadership.
- Weekly video/update language also appears in older NACo roles and Recent Projects; avoid repeating “first/recurring” claims unless differentiated.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skill block overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive value, not restate broad communications terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance, publishing systems & workflow design
- Cross-channel communications operations leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy, content planning & information architecture
- Consider reducing to 4 bullets to improve scanability and avoid padding.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing “messaging,” “planning,” and “leadership” styles.
- If possible, align wording to recent impact areas from 2022–present: governance, platform modernization, AI-enabled discovery, analytics-informed content operations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is also already covered in the header/Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent strengths and group tools into clearer capability themes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as capability-led, not platform-led: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if they are important for target roles; otherwise trim to avoid diluting your strongest recent experience.
- Replace “technical execution” jargon with more outcome-oriented phrasing where possible, e.g., “CMS modernization and front-end delivery” or “Web platform implementation and integration.”
- Keep this section shorter than Technical + IT; use it to signal strengths, not list every tool.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JavaScript/jQuery, API integrations, Airtable” are already covered in Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and recent project/work bullets.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-level capability and business impact, not repeat every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to strategic capability, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten to 5–7 items and prioritize senior-level strengths: “Measurement strategy & KPI design • Executive/leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI & Looker Studio • User behavior analysis (Microsoft Clarity) • SEO and digital performance optimization”
- Group tools instead of listing each separately to improve scanability and reduce redundancy.
- If you can support it elsewhere, hint at scale/impact through wording like “enterprise analytics infrastructure” or “decision-ready reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly all tools here duplicate “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- “Leadership reporting” also overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize delivery capability and recent leadership-level multimedia work rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools/tasks to outcomes and scope: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Consider adding scale/context if accurate: “Recurring advocacy programming” or “Virtual and hybrid event production” to connect to recent NACo work.
- Keep to 4 concise bullets max and avoid software/tool detail here since Premiere Pro etc. already appear elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; use “hybrid event delivery” or “multi-camera production systems” here instead.
- PTZ/studio details may be redundant with Technical + IT unless this section is positioned as operational leadership, not tools.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize primary CMS strength or add light proficiency context.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise architecture, migration, modular content builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, order by strength/relevance: put **Drupal** first and consider grouping the rest as supporting platforms.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If you’ve delivered notable outcomes in these systems, move those metrics to recent experience bullets rather than listing them here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or differentiating this one as platform names only.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight beside enterprise CMS tools unless it supports a specific recent project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus toward execution tools, e.g. **Front-End & Technical Implementation:** HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Standardize phrasing: use **REST/API integrations** instead of the broader “API integrations,” and consider dropping version numbers (**HTML, CSS, JavaScript**) unless other skills also use them.
- If accurate, add one higher-value modern item tied to recent work, such as **JSON**, **GA4 event implementation**, or **technical SEO**, instead of keeping this purely generic.
- Order by relevance/impact: JavaScript • REST/API integrations • GTM • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • HTML • CSS • jQuery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM may also overlap with analytics infrastructure; keep it here only if this section is meant to be hands-on tools.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly framed around automation/build systems vs collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to improve signal: “Automation & workflow design: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier” and “Project/collaboration systems: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp, Slack, Teams.”
- Consider renaming to “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems” so Slack/Teams feel intentional, not padded.
- Put highest-value tools first based on your recent work: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier should lead.
- If space allows elsewhere, add a qualifier tied to impact: “used to support cross-team publishing, campaign coordination, and operational workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if collaboration platforms are explicitly part of the category.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms to include, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength shown in recent roles: enterprise email operations and audience engagement systems. It should read as a capability area, not just a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/enterprise weight: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional context instead of only names: **Higher Logic (member email/newsletters) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation/segmentation) • Mailchimp (campaign email)**
- If you have metrics elsewhere, keep this section tool-focused and let work experience carry outcomes; otherwise avoid inflating with unsupported claims.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo newsletter bullets, so don’t add generic phrases like “email strategy” here unless tied to platform use.
- Avoid repeating automation language already covered under “Automation & Workflow Systems.”

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete scale or output you can add.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and cut generic verbs: replace “supporting the creation” / “strengthening workflows” with specific actions like “helped establish,” “standardized,” “produced,” “coordinated.”
- Add measurable outputs if available: number of livestreams, cadence/years of weekly videos, website refresh scope, channels supported, or team size.
- Draft rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, standardizing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating website/governance language already covered more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the distinctive “firsts,” scope, and program/policy support rather than broad content production.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten the first sentence to show business value: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives that supported county-focused programs and policy communications.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer outcome-oriented line: “Produced multimedia and digital content that translated research and policy work into member-facing communications.”
- If possible, add volume or reach: number of episodes, project count, audiences served, or teams/programs supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid overemphasizing video/multimedia here unless you can distinguish it from the later weekly video/livestream work.
